title: nnWNet: Rethinking the Use of Transformers in Biomedical Image Segmentation and Calling for a Unified Evaluation Benchmark
mechanism: W-shaped network that keeps global (transformer) and local (conv) features flowing continuously across multiple resolutions (HRNet-like), integrated into the nnU-Net framework for unified benchmarking.
adaptation: Drop-in nnU-Net trainer, so it runs on our splits with the same recipe as the nnU-Net and ResEnc arms; label-safe augmentation. Keeping a full-resolution stream suits 1 to 2 px cracks.
min_experiment: nnWNet on the module-grouped folds against nnU-Net org and ResEnc M; CV-mean crack relF1@2, crack IoU and E1 relF1@2. Kill: CV-mean crack relF1@2 not above ResEnc M by 1 fold SD.
evidence: R: state of the art claimed on 2D DRIVE (retinal vessels), ISIC-2017, Kvasir-SEG and CREMI (EM membranes), and on 3D Parse2022, AMOS22, BTCV, ImageCAS, against nnU-Net and transformer baselines. Exact DRIVE/CREMI numbers not retrieved.

alt_notes.adaptation: Run its 2D trainer on our nnU-Net dataset folder (1 channel, 512 px, 24 classes, label-safe aug, same folds). Hypothesis: the global stream separates long scuff streaks on half-cut E1 cells from local cracks while the conv stream keeps 1-2 px detail.
alt_notes.min_experiment: nnWNet 2D 5 folds v nnU-Net arm A winner and house 5-seed ensemble. Metric: E1 crack relF1@2 and recall, CV crack relF1@2. Kill if E1 relF1@2 < +0.03 over arm A and CV crack relF1@2 not up 0.01.
